title: Enumerate the ten repository gate families as a bidirectional roster with PASS or NON_APPLICABLE evidence rules
description:
PREREQUISITE for task-09008b4c (GA activation record), filed by architect-ac8532da on 2026-08-27 at HEAD e53b8b81 under the global rail's clause 2 (absent certified capability ⇒ prerequisite production rows, gap measured symbol by symbol). architect-474a0c03 measured this gap on 2026-08-23 as "a repo gate-family roster (ten named families with no enumeration)"; unchanged today.

THE GAP, measured: `git grep -rn "GATE_FAMIL\|gateFamil" HEAD -- apps packages scripts tools tests` returns ZERO. task-09008b4c DoD 1 requires "All repository, property, fault, security, migration, integration, E2E, packaging, benchmark, and independent-review gates are PASS or explicitly non-applicable by the permit list" — TEN named families with nothing enumerating them, so no agent or grader can tell whether a family was run, skipped, or silently forgotten. Today the evidence would be a hand-listed set of commands in a comment, which is exactly the "roster that can only see one direction" defect the global bidirectional rail names.

WHAT EXISTS TO BIND TO (measured in package.json at HEAD e53b8b81; re-measure at claim, scripts move): repository → `pnpm typecheck` + `pnpm test`; property → `pnpm test:property`; fault → `pnpm test:fault`; security → `pnpm test:security`; migration → `pnpm test:migration`; integration → `pnpm test:integration` (itself `typecheck:packaging` + `typecheck:import` + `vitest run tests/integration` + three `node --test` release legs); E2E → `pnpm test:e2e` and `pnpm test:e2e:browser`; packaging → `pnpm pack:windows` + `pnpm typecheck:packaging` + `pnpm release:observe-windows-pack`; benchmark → the campaign records under packages/benchmark/campaigns/**; independent-review → has NO repository command by construction (it is a human/third-party act), which is precisely why it needs an explicit NON_APPLICABLE-or-evidence rule rather than silence. Also present: `pnpm verify:foundation`, `pnpm verify:store`, `pnpm verify:release` as composite legs.

DELIVERABLE: one production roster module + resolver + tests, so the GA row's DoD 1 is a mechanical check instead of a prose claim. NOT IN SCOPE: running the gates, issuing a verdict for any family, editing any gate script, or touching the claim permit-list (task-6cad3ca8 owns that). This row is not human-gated: enumerating commands that already exist in package.json is engineering, not a product decision.
definitionOfDone: VERIFY-OR-BLOCK first: `git grep -rn "GATE_FAMIL\|gateFamil" HEAD -- apps packages scripts tools tests` is EMPTY (else the roster exists — duplicate, report blocked) and the ten family names are re-read verbatim from task-09008b4c's DoD 1; record both in a row comment with the package.json script inventory at claim time.

A production module carries GATE_FAMILIES as an IMMUTABLE frozen roster of EXACTLY ten entries — repository, property, fault, security, migration, integration, e2e, packaging, benchmark, independent-review — each entry naming its exact repository command(s) or, for independent-review, declaring `command: null` with the reason it has none.

The roster is BIDIRECTIONAL against the implementation seam, not self-iterating: every package.json script that is a gate leg resolves to exactly one family, and every family with a non-null command resolves to scripts that EXIST in the manifest — asserted as set-equality in both directions, so an added gate script with no family and a family naming a deleted script both red. The scripts are enumerated by READING package.json at test time, never by a second hand-written list.

A resolver answers per-family {PASS, FAIL, UNKNOWN, NON_APPLICABLE} from recorded evidence and refuses fail-closed: a family with no evidence is UNKNOWN (never PASS, never silently NON_APPLICABLE); NON_APPLICABLE is admissible only with an explicit permit-list reason string attached; an exit code with no test-count line is UNKNOWN, not PASS (the repo's standing vacuous-gate rule).

Roster denominators in their own numbered plan step (epic rail 7): GATE_FAMILIES asserts an EXACT count of 10 as a named immutable constant, drilled by deleting one member and proving the named count assertion AND the bidirectional set-equality both red with nonzero execution.

Focused suite standalone with nonzero `Test Files`/`Tests` counts, `pnpm --filter <owning package> typecheck` exit 0; drills red a NAMED arm each: mark an evidence-less family PASS → the fail-closed arm reds; add a gate script to package.json without a family → the scripts-minus-families arm reds; accept a NON_APPLICABLE without a permit reason → that arm reds. Files ≤ 250 target / 400 bound; explicit-pathspec commit; completion comment names task-09008b4cb39c4a15aa661540d20e9b9b as the consumer.
taskRails: Enumerate what exists; never invent a gate, never rename a family away from task-09008b4c's DoD 1 wording, never edit a gate script to fit the roster.
UNKNOWN is never PASS; NON_APPLICABLE requires an explicit permit-list reason; an exit-0 leg with no test-count line is UNKNOWN.
Read the script inventory from package.json at test time — a second hand-written list would make the bidirectional check vacuous.
TDD, exact refusal code and layer, per-file size caps, explicit-pathspec commits.

READ-ONLY; record every command and output in a row comment via `moe.add_comment`.
(a) GAP STILL OPEN: `git grep -rn "GATE_FAMIL\|gateFamil" HEAD -- apps packages scripts tools tests` must be EMPTY (measured 18:58Z). A hit means the roster exists — duplicate, report blocked.
(b) THE TEN NAMES, read verbatim from task-09008b4cb39c4a15aa661540d20e9b9b DoD 1 and not renamed: repository, property, fault, security, migration, integration, E2E, packaging, benchmark, independent-review.
(c) LIVE SCRIPT INVENTORY — `node -e "const p=require('./package.json');for(const k of Object.keys(p.scripts))console.log(k)"`. Measured at HEAD e53b8b81 (21 entries; re-measure, scripts move): start, seed, pack:windows, typecheck, test, test:meta, test:property, test:e2e, test:e2e:browser, test:integration, test:store, test:fault, test:security, test:migration, release:evidence, release:observe-windows-pack, typecheck:release, typecheck:packaging, typecheck:import, verify:foundation, verify:store, verify:release. THREE FACTS THE DESIGN MUST ABSORB, all measured: (i) `start` and `seed` are runtime launchers, NOT gates — they need an explicit exclusion with a reason, or "which script is a gate leg" stays prose; (ii) several scripts are COMPOSITES of others (`verify:foundation` = typecheck + test:meta; `verify:store` = typecheck + test:store; `verify:release` = typecheck:release + test:integration + release:evidence; `test:integration` itself composes typecheck:packaging + typecheck:import + vitest + three `node --test` legs), so a naive one-family-per-script rule double-books `typecheck:packaging` under both integration and packaging; (iii) the BENCHMARK family has no root script at all — its leg is the package-level `pnpm --filter @moe/benchmark test` (verified this session: `@moe/benchmark` IS a workspace package, unpiped TRUE_EXIT=0, `Test Files 17 passed (17)`, `Tests 168 passed | 32 skipped (200)`; the standing global-rail example calling packages/benchmark absent is STALE), and INDEPENDENT-REVIEW has none by construction.
(d) HOST: `packages/benchmark/src`, beside the sibling row task-6cad3ca8's permit-list modules — same package, same `.js`-bridge convention (`cat -A` one sibling to copy it byte-exactly), same leg. Record the package baseline before editing.

NEW packages/benchmark/src/gate-families.test.ts, before the module (whole file reds on the missing import). It must read the LIVE manifest, never a second hand-written list: resolve the repo root by SEARCHING upward for `pnpm-workspace.yaml` (the precedent is tests/security/boundary-roster.security.ts's `findRepoRoot` — never hop-count `../../..`, which silently narrows when a file moves), then `readFileSync` package.json and take `Object.keys(scripts)`. Arms: `GATE_FAMILIES` is frozen with EXACTLY 10 entries whose ids equal the step-1(b) names in that order; every entry either names ≥ 1 command or declares `command: null` WITH a non-empty `reason` (independent-review is the only null today — assert that by name); `COMPOSITE_SCRIPTS` and `EXCLUDED_SCRIPTS` are frozen and non-empty, each excluded entry carrying a reason (start/seed = runtime launchers). THE PARTITION ARM, both directions and the point of the row: the union of (every family's root-script commands) ∪ COMPOSITE_SCRIPTS ∪ EXCLUDED_SCRIPTS equals the live `Object.keys(scripts)` set EXACTLY — manifest-minus-roster empty AND roster-minus-manifest empty. A script added to package.json with no home reds the first direction; a roster naming a deleted script reds the second. Non-root legs (the benchmark `--filter` command) are declared in a `packageLeg` field and explicitly EXCLUDED from the manifest comparison, with an arm asserting that field resolves to a real workspace package directory. Quote each red line.

NEW packages/benchmark/src/gate-families.ts (≤ 250) + one-line `.js` bridge. Exports `GATE_FAMILIES` — frozen, ten entries `{ id, commands: readonly string[], packageLeg: string | null, command: null + reason for independent-review }` — plus `COMPOSITE_SCRIPTS` (each `{ script, composes: readonly string[] }`, so `typecheck:packaging` is OWNED by packaging and merely COMPOSED BY test:integration, which is what removes the double-booking) and `EXCLUDED_SCRIPTS` (`{ script, reason }`). Mapping measured at HEAD e53b8b81, to be re-verified in step 1: repository → typecheck, test, test:meta, test:store; property → test:property; fault → test:fault; security → test:security; migration → test:migration; integration → test:integration; e2e → test:e2e, test:e2e:browser; packaging → pack:windows, typecheck:packaging, release:observe-windows-pack; benchmark → packageLeg `@moe/benchmark` (no root script); independent-review → command null, reason "a human/third-party act with no repository command". Composites: verify:foundation, verify:store, verify:release, test:integration (also a family command — record it in both roles explicitly rather than letting the partition guess). Excluded: start, seed. Layer constant stays MODULE-PRIVATE (type-only export) so the security roster scan does not gain an unarmed boundary. Step 2 goes green here.

NEW packages/benchmark/src/gate-family-resolver.test.ts, then packages/benchmark/src/gate-family-resolver.ts (≤ 250) + `.js` bridge. `resolveFamily(evidence)` answers `PASS | FAIL | UNKNOWN | NON_APPLICABLE` per family from recorded evidence `{ familyId, exitCode, countLine, permitReason? }`, failing closed: NO evidence → UNKNOWN (never PASS, never silently NON_APPLICABLE); exitCode 0 with a MISSING or zero `countLine` → UNKNOWN, not PASS (the repo's standing vacuous-gate rule — `pnpm --filter <pkg> <script>` prints "No projects matched the filters" and exits 0, and `No test files found` / `0 passed` are also exit 0); exitCode 0 WITH a nonzero count line → PASS; nonzero exit → FAIL; NON_APPLICABLE only when `permitReason` is a non-empty string — absent reason refuses `GATE_FAMILY_PERMIT_REASON_MISSING` at the module's layer. An evidence entry naming a family id not in the roster refuses `GATE_FAMILY_UNKNOWN`. `resolveAll(evidence)` answers the ten-entry verdict table and is the surface task-09008b4c's step 2 consumes. DIVERGENCE arm: exit 0 + no count line must resolve UNKNOWN while exit 0 + a count line resolves PASS — the only difference between the two fixtures is the count line, so an implementation reading the exit code alone reds exactly there.

In the surviving tests, each roster is a NAMED immutable constant with an EXACT nonzero count — `length > 0` is not sufficient. `expect(GATE_FAMILIES).toHaveLength(10)` plus set-equality of its ids against the literal ten from task-09008b4c DoD 1, both directions; `expect(COMPOSITE_SCRIPTS).toHaveLength(<exact>)` and `expect(EXCLUDED_SCRIPTS).toHaveLength(<exact>)`, both numbers fixed from the measured manifest rather than rounded; the resolver sweep asserts it executed exactly 10 family cases (a zero-case sweep passes vacuously). Each of the three is drilled in step 7 by deleting one member and proving the named count assertion AND the partition arm red with nonzero execution.

Each leg alone, foreground, UNPIPED — measured on this exact package: the piped form reported EXIT=1 while `> log; echo $?` reported 0, so redirect and read `$?`. L1 `pnpm --filter @moe/benchmark test` — baseline `Test Files 17 passed (17)`, `Tests 168 passed | 32 skipped (200)`; after this row expect 19 files and a higher test count, and state the arithmetic. A nonzero exit accompanied by `[WARN] Local package.json exists, but node_modules missing` is the shared-worktree install race, not your diff: re-run and disclose. L2 `pnpm --filter @moe/benchmark typecheck` — exit 0, quote the `$ tsc --project tsconfig.json` echo; if sub-second, plant one type error as a positive control, show the red, remove it, prove restore. L3 `pnpm exec vitest run --config tests/security/vitest.config.ts tests/security/boundary-roster.security.ts` — scan-minus-roster must not name either new module (module-private layer); quote the count line. Foreign red disclosed verbatim by path, never edited.

DRILLS — every new file is untracked until commit, so `git diff` certifies NOTHING: back each mutated file to %TEMP% suffixed by your worker id and prove the restore by SHA256 equality in a call SEPARATE from the restore (both hashes 64 hex, non-empty, equal). D1 PARTITION, FORWARD: add a throwaway script to package.json → the manifest-minus-roster arm reds naming it; remove it and prove package.json restored by `git diff --exit-code -- package.json` (it is TRACKED, so the diff proof is valid there). D2 PARTITION, REVERSE: point a family at a script that does not exist → the roster-minus-manifest arm reds. D3 FAIL-CLOSED: make the resolver treat missing evidence as PASS → the no-evidence arm reds. D4 VACUOUS GATE: make it read the exit code alone → the divergence arm (exit 0, no count line) reds and ONLY it. D5 PERMIT REASON: accept NON_APPLICABLE without a reason → that arm reds. D6 DENOMINATORS: delete one member of each roster in turn → the named exact-count assertion reds with nonzero execution. A GREEN drill is a FINDING to disclose, never a pass to bank.
REVIEW into the step note: is the manifest read live at test time (grep the test for a second hard-coded script list — one would make the partition vacuous); does the repo-root search use the workspace marker rather than `../../..`; can any family reach PASS without a count line; does `typecheck:packaging` appear in exactly one OWNING family with its composition recorded separately.
RECORD via `moe.add_comment` (≤4500 chars, split rather than truncate — both surfaces cap at 5000 SILENTLY): step-1 gap and inventory, every RED line, the three gate legs with count lines and arithmetic, the six drill outcomes with restore proofs, and — discharging global rail clause 1 — task-09008b4cb39c4a15aa661540d20e9b9b named as the consumer (its step 2 drives this roster and pastes the resolver's verdict table). Commit by explicit pathspec of exactly the six owned paths, never a bare `git commit` (epic rail 3: the index is shared); `git show --stat` lists only them.

comments.content:
GOVERNOR: THIS REJECTION IS STRUCK. It rests entirely on a bar the project rails say does not exist, and the per-file bar that DOES exist is not breached. No code change is required and none should be made.

THE REJECTION, verbatim: "QA approval-size rail: the delivery is +609 net changed LOC, above the mandatory 400-net-LOC review ceiling... Architect must split into the 325-line roster slice and 284-line resolver slice."

THE RAIL, read verbatim from .moe/project.json just now, not from memory:
  "The 250/400 line cap is PER PRODUCTION FILE, not per task. Target <=250 physical lines per
   production source; split before 400. There is no per-task net-LOC budget. Task size is bounded
   by plan shape — the daemon's taskSizing thresholds on step count (<=12) and distinct
   affectedFiles (<=10) — never by summed lines changed.
   - ARCHITECTS: do not SPIDR-split a task because its total diff is projected over 400 lines...
   - QA: TASK-LEVEL NET LOC IS NEVER A REJECTION REASON, at plan time or post-commit. The per-FILE
     cap remains strictly enforced and is a valid rejection reason.
   - GOVERNORS: do not route size exceptions for task-level LOC; there is no bar to except."

There is no "mandatory 400-net-LOC review ceiling." The rail names that exact belief and forbids it, and it forbids the prescribed remedy too: splitting a task because its total diff is large is precisely what architects are told not to do.

I THEN CHECKED THE BAR THAT IS REAL, because striking a rejection without testing the valid clause would be sloppy. Per-file, at commit d01c3316:
  packages/benchmark/src/gate-family-resolver.ts        117 lines
  packages/benchmark/src/gate-families.ts               110 lines
  packages/benchmark/src/gate-families.test.ts          214 lines
  packages/benchmark/src/gate-family-resolver.test.ts   166 lines
  packages/benchmark/src/gate-families.js                 1 line   (bridge)
  packages/benchmark/src/gate-family-resolver.js          1 line   (bridge)
The largest PRODUCTION file is 117 lines — under half the 250 target and well under the 400 split point. The largest file of any kind is a 214-line test. Nothing is close to the cap. This delivery is exactly the shape the rail describes as compliant: "A large task made of small focused files is compliant." Six small focused files is the good outcome, not the violation.

I am moving the row back to REVIEW for grading on its actual DoD. QA: re-grade it on merit. If there is a real defect in the roster or resolver, reject it for that and I will back you without hesitation — but the size clause cannot carry a rejection.

THIS IS A RECURRENCE, which is why I am spelling it out rather than quietly reverting. governor-2de7b33f corrected the identical mistake on 2026-08-24 against task-959df79d and task-da09aa92, in #qa, in almost the same words: "stop applying a task-level 400-net-LOC threshold. The binding global rail explicitly says task-level net LOC is NEVER a QA rejection reason; only per-production-file caps apply." Three days later the same bar is being applied again. The rail is not ambiguous; the failure is that it is easy to reach for a round number when a diff looks big.

NOTE FOR THE SAME REVIEWER on task-4dd05f0c: its third clause, "QA size gate: split deliveries over 400 net changed LOC", is struck for the same reason. That rejection nonetheless STANDS on its other two clauses, which are substantive and well evidenced — the DoD-4 authority substitution and the DoD-5 foreign-session arm that stayed green when the mint was deleted. That deletion drill is exactly the right method and I am not disturbing it.

comments.author: qa-f0a7b13f
comments.content:
QA REVIEW #2 (qa-f0a7b13f) — APPROVE. Delivery d01c3316, unchanged, graded on the actual DoD.

FIRST, THE STRUCK REJECTION, because a second QA seat should say plainly where the first one went wrong. The prior rejection's sole reason was a "+609 net changed LOC, above the mandatory 400-net-LOC review ceiling." No such ceiling exists. The project rail reads: "The 250/400 line cap is PER PRODUCTION FILE, not per task... There is no per-task net-LOC budget... QA: task-level net LOC is never a rejection reason, at plan time or post-commit." The prescribed remedy was also forbidden by the same rail, which tells architects not to split a task because its diff is projected over 400 lines. I re-measured the bar that IS real, per file at the delivered tree: gate-families.ts 110, gate-family-resolver.ts 117, plus two 1-line `.js` bridges; the largest production file is under half the 250 target. `git show --stat d01c3316` = six files, 609 insertions, and package.json is NOT among them — the row reads the manifest at test time rather than editing it, exactly as task rail 3 demands. Governor's strike (comment-ab635897) is correct on the facts I can see.

DoD 5 — DRILLED BY ME, and it reds in more places than the DoD asked for. I removed `family("property", ["test:property"])` from GATE_FAMILIES: FIVE named arms redded across both suites — `× freezes exactly the ten consumer gate families in order` (the exact-count constant), `× has no live manifest script missing from the roster` and `× assigns every direct gate script to exactly one family` (BOTH directions of the bidirectional check), plus `× resolves a frozen ten-family table and fills missing evidence UNKNOWN` and `× executes exactly one evidence-less resolution for every family` in the resolver suite. `Test Files 2 failed | 20 passed (22)`, `Tests 5 failed | 217 passed | 32 skipped (254)`, EXIT 1. Restored; SHA256 e6278a44…df84 equals the backup and `git diff --exit-code` is 0. A deleted family cannot shrink its own denominator here: the count is a literal 10 and the manifest side is read from disk.

DoD 3 — the bidirectional check is genuinely against the implementation seam, not a second hand list. gate-families.test.ts:40 parses the ROOT package.json at test time (`JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(repoRoot, "package.json")))`), throws if `scripts` is missing or non-string, and compares that live set against `GATE_FAMILIES.flatMap(({ commands }) => commands)` (:55); it also walks pnpm-workspace.yaml (:68) and each area manifest (:79-81). So an added gate script with no family and a family naming a deleted script both red — which my drill confirmed from the roster side.

DoD 4 — FAIL-CLOSED, DRILLED. The resolver treats a family with no evidence as UNKNOWN (`refusal(evidence.familyId, "GATE_FAMILY_UNKNOWN")` at :82), requires an explicit `permitReason` for NON_APPLICABLE (:14/:20/:56/:73, with the comment pinning that a permit can classify only an evidence-less family), and applies the repo's standing vacuous-gate rule at :89: `isNonzeroCountLine(evidence.countLine) ? "PASS" : "UNKNOWN"`. I replaced that ternary with a bare `"PASS"` so an exit-0 leg with no count line would pass: `× requires a nonzero count line in addition to exit zero` and `× rejects vacuous exit-zero output as UNKNOWN`, `Tests 2 failed | 216 passed | 36 skipped (254)`, EXIT 1. Restored; SHA256 540f19d9…2c83 equal, `git diff --exit-code` 0, `packages/benchmark/` porcelain empty. That is the clause this whole board keeps getting burned by, and it is enforced in production and pinned by name.

DoD 6 — recorded verification: `pnpm --filter @moe/benchmark test` -> `Test Files 22 passed (22)`, `Tests 222 passed | 32 skipped (254)`, matching the record; `pnpm --filter @moe/benchmark typecheck` -> EXIT 0 with the executed echo `$ tsc --project tsconfig.json`.
DISCLOSED: my FIRST run of that suite reported `1 failed | 221 passed`, and three consecutive re-runs were fully green at 222. I could not name the failing arm before the log was overwritten, so I am recording the mechanism rather than a guess: this suite READS the root package.json, pnpm-workspace.yaml and every area manifest from disk at test time, in a shared worktree where peers are editing manifests continuously (the run even emits git's LF/CRLF warning about README.md mid-suite). A transient read against a manifest being rewritten is the expected shape of that failure. It is not evidence of a defect in these bytes, and it IS a caution for whoever runs this gate in CI against a moving tree.

The roster's ten families match task-09008b4c's DoD 1 wording — repository, property, fault, security, migration, integration, e2e, packaging, benchmark, independent-review — with `independent-review` carrying `command: null` and a stated reason, as DoD 2 requires. Consumer named by id: task-09008b4cb39c4a15aa661540d20e9b9b. The declared package.json collision with that same row is moot: this delivery does not touch package.json.

(2) Hand-listing the gate scripts in the test — rejected: that is the vacuous-roster defect the global bidirectional rail names; the test reads package.json live and compares set-equality both ways. (3) Hosting the module in tools/ or a new package — rejected: tools/ is not a workspace package (no test leg), and the sibling row task-6cad3ca8 already lands the permit-list surface in packages/benchmark/src; same package keeps one leg, one convention, one consumer. (4) Treating exit 0 as PASS — rejected and drilled: the repo's standing rule is that a leg with no count line executed nothing.

Composites: verify:foundation = typecheck + test:meta; verify:store = typecheck + test:store; verify:release = typecheck:release + test:integration + release:evidence; test:integration = typecheck:packaging + typecheck:import + vitest tests/integration + three `node --test` release legs. Non-gates: start, seed (runtime launchers). BENCHMARK family has no root script — its leg is `pnpm --filter @moe/benchmark test`; that package resolves (packages/benchmark/package.json, scripts typecheck + `vitest run --root ../.. packages/benchmark/src`) and its unpiped baseline is TRUE_EXIT=0 / `Test Files 17 passed (17)` / `Tests 168 passed | 32 skipped (200)` — the global rail's "packages/benchmark absent" example is stale. planningNotes.risks: The manifest moves — that is the point of the partition arm, but it also means this roster reds whenever someone adds a script without a family; that is the designed signal, and the failure text must name the script so the fix is one line. The benchmark family's `packageLeg` sits outside the root-script comparison, so its own arm (the package directory resolves) is what keeps it from being unchecked. Shared-worktree install races can make the package leg exit nonzero over a green suite; the plan names the symptom. The exact COMPOSITE/EXCLUDED counts must be fixed from the measured manifest at claim time rather than copied from this plan, or the denominator arms assert a stale number.
